newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor chairman favours current stakes - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Investor chairman favours current stakes - magazine.

text.p: The new chairman of Swedish investment company Investor, Percy Barnevik, sees higher return on current holdings as the company's main potential, magazine Veckans Affarer reported on Monday.
"If you are good at taking care of cyclical matters, it is a competitive advantage to have a cyclical structure," Barnevik was quoted as saying.
"Take (engineer) Asea/ABB. The company is cyclical in a slowly growing sector but the share has risen 54 times since 1980, almost three times more than the index."
"The largest upside in Investor is to get more from what is already there."
Barnevik is chairman of ABB and was recently proposed as chairman of Investor, the key investment vehicle of the Swedish Wallenberg family of financiers.
Barnevik told the weekly that companies such as engineer Atlas Copco, appliance maker Electrolux and bearing maker SKF should have strong potential.
But he said he expected Investor in the future to buy stakes in fast-growing sectors such as medical technology, automation and possibly also information technology.
Barnevik told the weekly there could be changes in bank S-E-Banken, in which Investor has doubled its stake to 9.2 percent of capital this year.
"The aim is to do something positive with the bank," he was quoted as saying.
"Then you cannot own a few percent of the shares, you need to have an ownership position. We have among other things pointed to asset management. I cannot say more."
The Swedish bank sector has seen large restructuring this year with Handelsbanken taking over mortgage lender Stadshypotek and Swedbank announcing it would merge with Foreningsbanken.
Speculation about a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken took off last autumn, but merger talks broke down earlier this year. Analysts expect the banks to resume talks.
